So now I need to pay for both an electrician and plumber to *possibly* return this machine to an operational state. Given my suspicion that the electrical components of the machine are now at least part of the issue as well, it is more practical and cost-effective to simply replace the machine with a brand new unit. But it will certainly not be an LG unit, and I feel I cannot risk purchasing any other LG products in the future. With a stated operational expectancy of 10 years, the failure of this machine after just 3 years was obviously very disappointing, and LG's failure to make it right makes me lose faith in their commitment to stand by the quality of their products. Additionally, a motor warranty that still requires a $200 out-of-pocket expenditure grants virtually no peace of mind for future purchases given this represents over 1/4 of the original cost. LG is just fortunate that the shorting machine did not start an electrical fire in my home as that would obviously have been a much larger problem, and represents a significant liability for their company.

However, it worked for only 20 days since it was installed. I bought this dishwasher on 11/7/23 from Menards for about $650, including delivery and pick up of the old dishwasher. Due to a mistake at Menards, the delivery was delayed a week. I had to reschedule the installer because of that delay. Once delivered, it was installed on 11/13/23, and it worked great until 11/27/23. The dishwasher would start and run but the wash arms did not turn. Nothing was clean. We verified all electrical connections and water connections. Sentence (English): The product is excellent, but you pay €29 to arrange a delivery day.
Comments (English): [ Excellent product, terrible delivery ] || ---------------- || The product is excellent, but you pay €29 to arrange a delivery day. On the agreed day the transport did not appear but I received an email that the product had been delivered. After 48 hours talking to customer service by email and phone, the transport company appears and leaves the device at the entrance of the house, no installation, they take three photos and run away without almost removing the old equipment. Ten minutes later, customer service notifies me that the product appears to have been delivered and there are photographs of it. Surreal!
Comments (Original): [ Excelente producto, pésima entrega ] || ---------------- || El producto es excelente, pero pagas 29€ para concertar un día de entrega.El día acordado el transporte no aparecío pero me llego un email de que el producto había sido entregado.Tras 48 horas hablando con atención al cliente por email y teléfono, la empresa de transporte aparece y deja el aparato en la entrada de casa, nada de instalación, hacen tres fotos y salen corriendo sin casi retirar el equipo viejo.Diez minutos después desde atención al cliente me notifican que el producto consta como entregado y hay fotografías de ello...Surrealista!!!

Sentence (English): It is the first dishwasher we have had and we are very happy, with a new member in the family the dirty dishes have increased and the time has been reduced, so we are delighted that someone washes for us!

The dishes come out much cleaner than I expected and I loved how good the rubber on the glass tupperware looks, which are difficult to clean by hand. As a criticism, I would say child blocking. It is not well thought out, it is true that it locks the machine during operation, but it does not lock it off so you can easily start it using only two buttons, it loves tapping on all the buttons with lights so it was an important feature for us , this has disappointed us since we have to be careful that it does not start. The lock should be enabled at all times as it happens in other appliances, it is for this point that I do not give it 5 stars since it was an issue that we reviewed during the purchase and ruled out other brands that did not have a lock.

Como crítica, diría el bloqueo infantil. No está bien pensado, es cierto que bloquea la máquina durante el funcionamiento, pero no la bloquea apagada por lo que la puede arrancar fácilmente usando sólo dos botones, le encanta tocar en todos los botones con luces por lo que era una función importante para nosotros, esto nos ha defraudado ya que tenemos que estar pendientes de que no la arranque. El bloqueo debería quedar habilitado en todo momento como ocurre en otros electrodomésticos, es por este punto que no le pongo las 5 estrellas ya que era un tema que revisamos durante la compra y descartamos otras marcas que no tenían bloqueo.

Sentence (English): While aesthetically I would give this 5 stars, practically I give it a 3.5.
Comments (English): [ It's pretty but.  ] || ---------------- || While aesthetically I would give this 5 stars, practically I give it a 3.5. We bought this mainly for looks when replacing all of our kitchen appliances and loved the sleek black look. According to the size it was the same as what it was replacing so we assumed we were mostly just getting an upgrade as far as efficiency and looks. It just FEELS so much smaller. I don't know why but it feels like everything just barely fits. We couldnt even use the very slim top tray because then our glassware wouldnt fit on the top, and we had to drop the "top" so now tall cooking utensils dont fit in the holder on the bottom - we still have to store them flat on the "top" but that is taking space away from the top-shelf wash only items. The only great thing about the functionality of this dishwasher is that it pops open after the cycle to allow air in to actually dry the dishes (instead of puddles on mug bottoms, etc.). If you are replacing for looks - I would highly recommend this! However, after using it a bit I would not recommend it for functionality. There are better dishwashers on the market that just dont look as sleek!

Sentence (English): We love this dishwasher.
Comments (English): We love this dishwasher. There is so much room. The third rack although shallow frees up so much room on the other two racks. We love the moveable second rack. The dishwasher also washes dishes exceptionally well even in the 'normal' mode. I would warn people that most of the functionality on this model is through the app. We found the app to be simple and think most people would. But that is something that maybe some might not like. One other warning is that this model only comes with the 120v electric plug option. If you want the direct wire option, it's a separate piece to order. Our old model was a direct electric wire so once the old one was out, I spent some time running back to Home Depot to get an electric box, outlet and cover, and an hour or so to install a 120v outlet. I wagered that was faster than ordering the direct wire conversion cord.

Sentence (English): We had the dishwater for 1 week before it displayed an HRF error code and would not function anymore.
Comments (English): We had the dishwater for 1 week before it displayed an HRF error code and would not function anymore. Of course this is past the 48 hour window to return the product so we have had to wait for a certified repairman to come service the dishwasher. When speaking with the GE customer service we were informed that someone local would be available to come within 2 weeks to service. At the conclusion of the 2 weeks we were informed by GE customer service that although someone would be available to service the washer, we were responsible for also individually contacting the service provider to schedule the appointment. We did this immediately. 3 weeks later(today) the repairman stopped by and informed there was a faulty relay and it would be 4-5 weeks before the part would come in and he would be back to service it. It's been 2 months since we ordered this dishwasher and still have to wait another month before we can use it! Stay away from this product.

We are quite disappointed.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher a few months ago and I can't say I'm really at all happy with it.
Comments (English): [ Not as happy as I was hoping ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher a few months ago and I can't say I'm really at all happy with it. I bought it because it was one of the only ones that fit my bowl plates (cross between the two). Unfortunately they only fit in one side at the back due to the tines in the other side being two different heights which means the bowls fall over and they can't stack at the front as they are slightly too big and sit at a weird angle. Due to the two different directions of the tines, forward facing at the back and sides to side at the front, you can't really fit a large chopping board in like the two rows of side to side can. Most things only fit in one spot and items in the back rows can actually get in the way of other items for to the fact that they lean into the front row. The adjustable tines don't lock firmly in place and feel flimsy and they move, again unlike my old one. The cup racks in the middle shelf are kinda removable but the bit they click into is molded into the drawer runner and sticks out, often in the way, and obviously can't be removed. The cups don't sit nicely against them either, as they don't seem to line up properly. The bottom rack has stoppers on it to prevent you pulling it out to far but ends up rolling back into dishwasher when you start to stack the back given that the door won't fold down anymore than it does (dishwasher was level and plumb when installed). And there is no off switch for the light. While it's good for popping dishes in late at night it's super annoying when the dishwasher pops the door open a little too far upon finishing and the light comes on wasting electricity. I also don't like that the door won't stay a tiny bit open to breathe but be out of the way. It's either closed or open about 20cm which means you are quite likely to walk into it. I do like the cutlery tray and how it has dividers to separate the forks & knives etc. And I like the height in the bottom as it can for a decent sized dinner plate. Rice style bowls don't stack well however and 8 can take up more than half the bottom rack of the dishwasher. Given that this dishwasher was the top of the range for this style I'm disappointed especially given how much research (and actually testing with my crockery) I did when choosing which one to buy. I really wish I hadn't bothered spending the extra money and I'd just straight replaced my old Bosch with a new one, basically the same, for half the price.

Sentence (English): Two drawers that are different sizes is perfection!
Comments (English): [ Perfection! in a dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Two drawers that are different sizes is perfection! If you have a small load, like we do most of the time with just two people, you can use the small drawer and it is very convenient. Larger, or dirtier, loads can be done in the larger drawer. I do like that you can run both drawers independently of each other and at the same time. The drawer and rack design is great as it allows flexibility in how you load, and the side movable shelves are genius and very handy. Given that there is only a bottom washer arm, you do have to load with that in mind, but it hasn't been an issue so far. Sentence (English): I debated it a hundred times before buying it.
Comments (English): [ Why did I worry? ] || ---------------- || I debated it a hundred times before buying it. It wasn't even expensive, so I wonder why I hesitated. Since I'm a weekend couple, it's mostly just me and my child, and even though I only cook dinner for the kids at home, the dishes still pile up little by little. The sink gets surprisingly full. After coming home from work, cooking, feeding, and cleaning up... when I saw the sink overflowing, I'd think, "Should I do it tomorrow? Or later?" and keep putting it off. The night I ordered this was truly, truly an exhausting day. So, seeing the overflowing sink, I just went ahead and bought it. Delivery was... The installation technician contacted me the day after I ordered. They said they couldn't do it that day but could install it the next day, so we scheduled a time. (Why is the technician so kind?) Installation time was... It seems to take about 20 minutes; I think it might take 30 minutes if you drill a hole. Since they worked through the existing water purifier hole, I didn't have to drill a separate hole. Cleaning power is... What more can I say about the cleaning power? Squeaky clean and piping hot—I realized I must have been eating a lot of germs all this time. Frying pans, pots, glass cups, spoons, and chopsticks all came out perfectly clean. I had purchased dishwasher detergent and rinse aid in advance, so I used it right away as soon as it arrived. I bought both liquid detergent and rinse aid. The technician told me that using rinse aid is a must. *****Pros*****. Putting everything else aside, I bought this because I considered whether the door opens automatically or not. I'd go for a more basic model. Fewer bells and whistles (which don't work all that well), same important Bosch features.

Well designed with 3 racks but top rack can't hold all flatware plus water bottle tops for a family of 5 after 1 day of use. Had to buy a clean/dirty magnet because when cycle is completed, no way of knowing for sure that dishes have been cleaned. If you're like me you don't want another app on your phone. I'd go for a more basic model. Fewer bells and whistles (which don't work all that well), same important Bosch features.

Sentence (English): This Bosch Benchmark Series dishwasher cleans MUCH better than our 2021 LG model, supposedly one of LG's best at the time.
Comments (English): This Bosch Benchmark Series dishwasher cleans MUCH better than our 2021 LG model, supposedly one of LG's best at the time. The LG left remnants of food plus a film on our kitchenware, even when using the heaviest wash cycle. We also performed all of the LG recommended filter & spray-arm cleaning, but that made no difference.The lighted interior of the LG stupidly turns off within seconds after opening to load, where the Bosch stays on for several minutes, plenty of time for loading.Also annoyed by the whining drone of the drying fan in the LG. Bosch's Crystal Dry also circulates air, but the fan is nearly silent.Only issue with the Bosch is the flimsy mounting brackets. 2 flat pieces of metal that bend and flex easily. Had to knock off a star since the unit wiggles back & forth in the cabinet opening, even after firmly screwing the brackets in place. Not happy about that.Cabinet mounting issues aside, this Bosch does an excellent job of cleaning. We no longer have to prewash everything like we did with our LG, happy about that.

We also performed all of the LG recommended filter & spray-arm cleaning, but that made no difference.The lighted interior of the LG stupidly turns off within seconds after opening to load, where the Bosch stays on for several minutes, plenty of time for loading.Also annoyed by the whining drone of the drying fan in the LG. Bosch's Crystal Dry also circulates air, but the fan is nearly silent.Only issue with the Bosch is the flimsy mounting brackets. 2 flat pieces of metal that bend and flex easily. Had to knock off a star since the unit wiggles back & forth in the cabinet opening, even after firmly screwing the brackets in place. Not happy about that.Cabinet mounting issues aside, this Bosch does an excellent job of cleaning. We no longer have to prewash everything like we did with our LG, happy about that.

The rack layouts had some positives, notably the reorienting of the lower front rack tines to prevent plates from moving when the rack rolls in and out. But, there is less customizable options in the tines. Plus, the layout doesn't work well for my 6" square plates. The upper rack is also less customizable. But appears to be able to accommodate more dishes. Unfortunately, I now get an intermittent error on drainage on the new system. It's not something I have figured out why yet.

Sentence (English): [This review was collected as part of a promotion.]
Comments (English): [ Excellent choice but less robust than before ] || ---------------- || [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We purchased this specific dishwasher model after viewing a popular consumer protection magazine that compared several models from different brands. Some models were more recommended but an important criterion for us was the quality of drying of plastic items and those coated with a non-stick surface. We are not disappointed. The result is excellent. The device washes very well and we love the 3rd basket and its 2 rotating cylinders from which the water springs. We place glasses and cups there. The side for long utensils lacks a little clearance from the ceiling. When it comes to the quality of construction materials, that’s another story. The sheets are thin and the frame does not have the rigidity of the kitchen models built 13 years ago; if the space at the top of the dishwasher is too tight, the pressure exerted by the insulation risks deforming the structure and hindering the closing of the door which will no longer coincide perfectly with the opening. Lower the height of the dishwasher if it fits too closely under the counter. There is also a large piece of transparent plastic on the side of the device which does not inspire confidence in me in terms of robustness and possible replacement cost. Something that is a little annoying is the presence of the control panel on the top . I have no fear of humidity because the fan outlet is at the bottom. However, inevitably we accidentally press a key from time to time. It gets annoying to the point of regretting not having the controls on the front. The plastic of the utensil basket doesn't seem very sturdy. From the way we place the sharp knives, I believe it will do like the one from the previous dishwasher which was replaced twice.Conclusion: I believe it is one of the best choices on the market in terms of good product that its price is higher. My sister-in-law also bought the same model a few months before us and she is delighted with it.
Comments (Original): [ Excellent choix mais moins robuste qu’autrefois ] || ---------------- || [Cet avis a été recueilli dans le cadre d’une promotion.] Nous avons acheté précisément ce modèle de lave-vaisselle après avoir consulté un magazine populaire de protection des consommateurs qui comparait plusieurs modèles de marques différentes. Certains modèles étaient davantage recommandés mais un critère important pour nous était la qualité du séchage des article de plastique et ceux revêtus d’une surface anti adhésive.Nous ne sommes pas déçus. Le résultat est excellent. L’appareil lave très bien et nous adorons le 3e panier et ses 2 cylindres rotatifs d’où l’eau jaillit. Nous y plaçons verres et tasses. Le côté pour les longs ustensiles manque un peu de dégagement avec le plafond. Côté qualité des matériaux de construction, c’est une autre histoire. Les tôles sont minces et l’armature n’a pas la rigidité des modèles kitchen construits il y a 13 ans; si l’espace en haut du lave-vaisselle est trop serré, la pression exercée par l’isolant risque déformer la structure et de nuire à la fermeture de la porte qui ne coïncidera plus parfaitement avec l’ouverture. Sentence (English): The Bosch 800 series dishwasher has exceeded my expectations.
Comments (English): The Bosch 800 series dishwasher has exceeded my expectations. It has been one month and I have used about 40 cycles. (I know this because I downloaded the App and connected it to my wifi.) The App also notifies you when cycles are finished. There is also a red light that illuminates the floor at the bottom right to also let you know when it's running if you don't download the App, otherwise it's very quiet and you can't tell if it's running. The automatic is the best setting so far because it adjusts the cleaning time (mostly 1hr 40 min to 2 hours) based on the level of dirtiness. The half full cycle is also a great feature to save water. The 60 minute is a lifesaver when you have more than a sink full of dishes. It completely cleans your dishes, but not completely dry, more dry than you'd expect in a short cycle. When I place dishes and pots into dishwasher where I have just wiped away excess food particles, they come out clean, so no water rinse is needed! Bosch does not disappoint as the dishes come out squeaky clean, even if food is dried on. Starchy residue also comes off, even if it's dried on! I believe that is the point, save water and let the dishwasher do the cleaning. I do use the recommended jet dry cleaning pod as well as the rinse agent. In addition, Bosch included a water hardness tester. My water was borderline hard and decided to buy and added the 'dishwasher salt'. There are no water spots, however there were none before I added the 'salt'. One thing to note, the new drying element does not 'melt' nor warp my plastic Tupperware containers or lids. One thing to note, there are times when a small amount of water might pool on the top of 1or 2 cups, but I think I have to make sure they are on an angle when loading. The only thing I would change about the dishwasher is the second level configuration. The design doesn't allow for the placement of many glasses because they've added a section to place long stem glassses. I believe the inside is also a little bit smaller than standard dishwashers (even though this one is standard), however overall dimensions/size is the same. Overall, I would 100% buy this 800 series Bosch again and give it 5 stars! Highly recommend! The gentleman (assigned by Costco) who installed the dishwasher were quick and very professional!

Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ SHE3AEM5N ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I had an old Bosch 50db machine (12 years old) that I replaced with this one. I kept the insulating wrap from the old one and placed on new machine as it didn't come with any insulating wrap. It's fairly quiet however on some portions of the cycle there is still noise through the door. I think a little insulation inside the door would go a long way to muffle the noise and at minimal cost to Bosch. The top rack is positioned a little lower and it works well to accommodate larger items. However, missing is the capability on the top rack to fold down a section of tangs which I had on the old machine and I miss. The bottom came with two silverware baskets that don't fit well. I have used the old single long silverware basket from my old machine which fits and stays put. The old machine had a clean lamp indicator light that stayed lit until you opened the door. This new model does not offer that feature which is also disappointing. Instead, it sends a notice to your mobile phone to tell you the wash cycle is done, so one person in the house knows the dishes are clean. I would rather have an indicator lamp so anyone looking at the machine can see the dishes are clean. We bought the stainless steel model and there is a plastic film that has to be removed. There is no information in the manual or documentation that tells you it can be removed. Also it was very difficult to pull it off.

It took a bit of time to understand which buttons we needed to push to get the desired result and we have pretty much stuck to one set of washing cycles.

Sentence (English): I had an old Bosch 50db machine (12 years old) that I replaced with this one.
Comments (English): [ SHE3AEM5N ] || ---------------- || I had an old Bosch 50db machine (12 years old) that I replaced with this one. I kept the insulating wrap from the old one and placed on new machine as it didn't come with any insulating wrap. It's fairly quiet however on some portions of the cycle there is still noise through the door. I think a little insulation inside the door would go a long way to muffle the noise and at minimal cost to Bosch. The top rack is positioned a little lower and it works well to accommodate larger items. However, missing is the capability on the top rack to fold down a section of tangs which I had on the old machine and I miss. The bottom came with two silverware baskets that don't fit well. I have used the old single long silverware basket from my old machine which fits and stays put. The old machine had a clean lamp indicator light that stayed lit until you opened the door. This new model does not offer that feature which is also disappointing. Instead, it sends a notice to your mobile phone to tell you the wash cycle is done, so one person in the house knows the dishes are clean. I would rather have an indicator lamp so anyone looking at the machine can see the dishes are clean. We bought the stainless steel model and there is a plastic film that has to be removed. There is no information in the manual or documentation that tells you it can be removed. Also it was very difficult to pull it off.

Comments (English): [ Wow, I like it ] || ---------------- || This is a product I really wanted. Manufacturing date: Nov. 2, 2023 / Installation date: Dec. 6, 2023. I missed the lowest price a few weeks ago and bought it for 50,000 won more, but since I was starting to get stressed about the pile of dishes after cooking, I really needed a dishwasher lady. They say there isn't much difference from the new model. In fact, I actually bought the 2023 model but canceled it because I heard the 2023 model only added baby bottle sterilization and drying functions. So, I am satisfied with this product. Additional review: After using it for a few days, dishwashing time has definitely decreased by 20-30 minutes. I rinse things roughly and put them in, but if you put in hard rice grains without soaking them first, they don't get cleaned properly. You have to soak and wash dishes that are stuck tightly, just like you normally would. A 28cm frying pan fits inside. I ate dinner late at night, ran the wash cycle, and went to sleep, and by morning, it was almost completely dry. It wasn't dry when I opened it right away, but I am still satisfied at this level. I am preparing to buy one at my parents' house as well. However, since unit prices on Coupang fluctuate so much, you have to grab it when the price seems low. After watching prices for a few weeks to decide which one to buy, I found that the cheapest price was in the high 200s. I use Frog Detergent, and since I fill it almost to the brim with dishes, I only use about half the capacity. Some say you can fill it up to a third if you don't have enough, but it gets packed full with pots, dishes, bowls, and all sorts of other things. The most important thing is that when stacking dishes (pots, bowls), you must put them in at an angle, not upside down. This is necessary for the detergent and water to be absorbed and for drying to occur. I think that is how you should load them. One day, I thought I had put a pot in at an angle, but it was sitting upright, and the rinse water had just piled up, which was ridiculous. Please keep this in mind!

Sentence (English): Very good dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Versatile, connected and efficient ] || ---------------- || Very good dishwasher. It's not easy to compare it with other brands because I've only had Bosch (including the old one). The washing is impeccable, no complaints. I appreciated the connected function which allows you to configure everything from the application. But my favorite function remains the automatic door opening which allows me to no longer have to wait until the end to go to bed, for example. The door opens by itself once the program is finished and that's very nice! (The instructions should have been clearer on this subject because it was poorly explained and it took me a while to understand that it was necessary to activate the "EfficientDry" option in the general settings). I was doubtful about the cutlery drawer, that's why I bought an optional Bosch basket, but as a result I use the drawer for other items and it's very practical. The only downside is that I expected it to be quieter than my old Bosch which was an old built-in model, but the difference in noise is not huge. Another fault also: I find that even the "Express" program is still a little long (1h30 minimum if I remember correctly) and my old model did just as well in much less time because I had a 45 min program I believe. The height adjustment system for the feet could also have been a little more qualitative and better thought out, it was tedious to square everything. To return to noise, there is however an optional silence mode for those teleworking in an open room for example. But the washing remains impeccable and that is what we mainly ask of it. The overall quality printing is also there. It is also very practical to have the buttons on the edge of the door so you do not have to bend down to program. Overall, I remain very satisfied, especially since the price difference with the Series 6 was not huge. So I opted for this excellent series 8. Hoping that the reliability is there too ;-)
Comments (Original): [ Polyvalent, connecté et performant ] || ---------------- || Très bon lave vaisselle. Pas évident de le comparer avec d'autres marques car je n'ai eu que du Bosch (y compris l'ancien). Le lavage est impeccable, rien à redire. J'ai apprécié la fonction connectée qui permet de tout paramétrer depuis l'application. Mais ma fonction préférée reste l'ouverture de porte automatique qui me permet de ne plus avoir à attendre la fin pour aller me coucher par exemple. La porte s'ouvre toute seule une fois le programme fini et c'est très appréciable ! (La notice aurait méritée d'être plus clair d'ailleurs à ce sujet car c'était mal expliqué et j'ai mis du temps à comprendre qu'il fallait activer l'option 'EfficientDry' dans les paramètres généraux). J'étais dubitatif sur le tiroir à couvert, c'est pour cela que j'ai acheté un panier Bosch optionnel, mais du coup j'utilise le tiroir pour d'autres éléments et c'est bien pratique.Seul bémol, je m'attendais à ce qu'il soit plus silencieux que mon ancien Bosch qui était un vieux modèle encastrable, mais la différence de bruit n'est pas énorme. Autré défaut également : je trouve que même le programme 'Express' est tout de même un peu long (1h30 minimum si je me souviens bien) et mon vieux modèle faisait tout aussi bien en beaucoup moins de temps car j'avais un programme 45 min je crois.Le système de réglage en hauteur des pieds aurait pu également être un peu plus qualitatif et mieux pensé, c'était fastidieux de tout mettre d'équerre... Pour revenir au bruit, Il existe cependant un mode silence optionnel pour ceux en télétravail dans une pièce ouverte par exemple. Mais le lavage demeure impeccable et c'est ce qu'on lui demande principalement. L'impression de qualité générale est également au rendez-vous.Il est aussi très pratique d'avoir les boutons sur la tranche de la porte pour ne pas avoir à se baisser pour la programmation.Dans l'ensemble je reste donc très satisfait surtout que l'écart de prix avec la série 6 n'était pas faramineux. J'ai donc opté pour cette excellente série 8. En espérant que la fiabilité soit au rendez-vous également ;-)

Sentence (English): What is good about this Bosch is that it has a built in leak detector if the pump fails, and will keep the leak constrained to within the dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Very Quiet, Fixes Issue In Last Years Model ] || ---------------- || What is good about this Bosch is that it has a built in leak detector if the pump fails, and will keep the leak constrained to within the dishwasher. If the water inlet connection fails however (for example if you didn't tighten the connection enough or the connection fails), you will still have a leak. For that reason I have installed wifi enabled leak detectors that I have put underneath the water inlet connection. These are silent (so my dog wont hear) and will alert me with a notification on an app if it leaks.As far as the rest of the dishwasher, this new model has a heat shield for the water distribution manifold, which in last years equivalent model, was susceptible to being damaged by the crystal dry vent. My last Bosch failed this way (identical model but last years model, only lasted 2 years) but I bought this Bosch again because of the built in leak protection. Every other brand of dishwasher I have had the pump always fails and leaks water ruining my floor. The leak pan prevents this from happening but you still need the wifi sensors I mentioned above to detect all leaks.This is the sweet spot in the Bosch lineup in my opinion. The best feature is the third tray on the top which is extremely useful. This years model also comes with app control to let you start the dishwasher and monitor the cycle (you can find out how many minutes are left in the cycle for example).

Comments (English): [ $800 Boat Anchor ] || ---------------- || This review WAS NOT collected as part of a promotion! Steer clear! This unit is advertised as "No Rinse", well, that's a total lie. Given the multiple failings of this unit, I doubt it sanitizes. But, how would you ever know for sure. Seems like an non-testable promise. Again, if you like crusty dinnerware and completely pre-washing. well, this baby is for you!

Comments (English): [ Covered not covered ] || ---------------- || The mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area from the bottom rotating sprayer, along the floor of the wash area, up the back wall of the wash area to the top rotating sprayer had a leak. The heat weakens the mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area causing it to fail (puts a hole in the side of the supply line). The third-party rep said it is an ongoing problem and there is an unofficial recall.He came back a week later and installed a new mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area. This new one has a protective sleeve to prevent the problem.I almost went out and bought a new dishwasher, and it wasn't going to be a Bosh.PS this happened almost three years to the date that installed the dishwasher. The repair cost me time - something move valuable than money. I am happy now. Mostly because it didn't have to waste any more time. Ironically, I'm wasting time writing this :) Hope it helps someone.

Comments (English): [ I am satisfied with my LG dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || (Buy with my own money) I bought a new dishwasher when I moved! I'm very satisfied :) When I moved, I left my old dishwasher behind and bought a new one for my new home! My old one was a Chef*Rexion, but this time I wanted an LG dishwasher! Even though I use a good dishwasher, I only use standard models, so I checked the price range and ordered it on Coupang! The white color matches my current kitchen! My previous owner also had an LG dishwasher, so I had a spare. The technician just installed it. I'll compare it to my old dishwasher. LG. *3-tier structure - 2 turntables (bottom, middle). The top one seems to only dispense water. *Cutlery and utensil wash compartments are on the top (they wash individual spoons and chopsticks). *Buttons are located on the front, near the handle. *The lower plate compartment folds down (making it easy to load pots). *There's a separate compartment for solid detergent. My previous dishwasher: * Two-tier structure with three rotating water jets (top, middle, bottom). * Separate cutlery drawers, placed in the bottom compartment (making it impossible to wash each spoon separately). * Buttons are on the top of the handle. * The lower plate compartment doesn't fold (you have to play Tetris to place pots in it). * Since there's only one place to put the cutlery, you have to put both solids and liquids in the same place (they sometimes fall out). There were some big differences for me. First, the buttons! The buttons on the LG one are a bit inconvenient. They're on the front and are touch-sensitive, so while I was cleaning the kitchen, I touched them and must have kept touching the cancel button. It canceled, so I had to restart the cycle. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. It also has a high-temperature drying function. The installer, an LG engineer, called to coordinate a date and installed the machine. I'm satisfied. It's not necessarily true that more expensive models have better cleaning power. If you're going to buy a model without a filter, I recommend it. Time: LG's standard was 1 hour and 33 minutes. The old one was 1 hour and 10 minutes. Both had automatic door opening. Cleaning power seems similar depending on the detergent used. Both products are linked to an app, so I get notifications when they're in use. I live in a new apartment, so I bought the filter-less model. I know models with filters are coming out these days, but the filter's value can't be ignored. I use it by heating it with cold water when washing, so I'm confident there won't be any issues. The only inconvenience is the front button, but I've been using it without any other issues. Electricity costs are similar for both models, since I use them every day.

My previous dishwasher: * Two-tier structure with three rotating water jets (top, middle, bottom). * Separate cutlery drawers, placed in the bottom compartment (making it impossible to wash each spoon separately). * Buttons are on the top of the handle. * The lower plate compartment doesn't fold (you have to play Tetris to place pots in it). * Since there's only one place to put the cutlery, you have to put both solids and liquids in the same place (they sometimes fall out). There were some big differences for me. First, the buttons! The buttons on the LG one are a bit inconvenient. They're on the front and are touch-sensitive, so while I was cleaning the kitchen, I touched them and must have kept touching the cancel button. It canceled, so I had to restart the cycle. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. It's not necessarily true that more expensive models have better cleaning power. If you're going to buy a model without a filter, I recommend it. Time: LG's standard was 1 hour and 33 minutes. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. Even though I use a good dishwasher, I only use standard models, so I checked the price range and ordered it on Coupang! The white color matches my current kitchen! My previous owner also had an LG dishwasher, so I had a spare. The technician just installed it. I'll compare it to my old dishwasher. LG. *3-tier structure - 2 turntables (bottom, middle). The top one seems to only dispense water. *Cutlery and utensil wash compartments are on the top (they wash individual spoons and chopsticks). *Buttons are located on the front, near the handle. *The lower plate compartment folds down (making it easy to load pots). *There's a separate compartment for solid detergent. My previous dishwasher: * Two-tier structure with three rotating water jets (top, middle, bottom). * Separate cutlery drawers, placed in the bottom compartment (making it impossible to wash each spoon separately). * Buttons are on the top of the handle. * The lower plate compartment doesn't fold (you have to play Tetris to place pots in it). * Since there's only one place to put the cutlery, you have to put both solids and liquids in the same place (they sometimes fall out). There were some big differences for me. First, the buttons! The buttons on the LG one are a bit inconvenient. They're on the front and are touch-sensitive, so while I was cleaning the kitchen, I touched them and must have kept touching the cancel button. It canceled, so I had to restart the cycle. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. It also has a high-temperature drying function. The installer, an LG engineer, called to coordinate a date and installed the machine. I'm satisfied. It's not necessarily true that more expensive models have better cleaning power. If you're going to buy a model without a filter, I recommend it. Time: LG's standard was 1 hour and 33 minutes. My previous owner also had an LG dishwasher, so I had a spare. The technician just installed it. I'll compare it to my old dishwasher. LG. *3-tier structure - 2 turntables (bottom, middle). The top one seems to only dispense water. *Cutlery and utensil wash compartments are on the top (they wash individual spoons and chopsticks). *Buttons are located on the front, near the handle. *The lower plate compartment folds down (making it easy to load pots). *There's a separate compartment for solid detergent. My previous dishwasher: * Two-tier structure with three rotating water jets (top, middle, bottom). * Separate cutlery drawers, placed in the bottom compartment (making it impossible to wash each spoon separately). * Buttons are on the top of the handle. * The lower plate compartment doesn't fold (you have to play Tetris to place pots in it). * Since there's only one place to put the cutlery, you have to put both solids and liquids in the same place (they sometimes fall out). There were some big differences for me. First, the buttons! The buttons on the LG one are a bit inconvenient. They're on the front and are touch-sensitive, so while I was cleaning the kitchen, I touched them and must have kept touching the cancel button. It canceled, so I had to restart the cycle. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. It's not necessarily true that more expensive models have better cleaning power. If you're going to buy a model without a filter, I recommend it. Time: LG's standard was 1 hour and 33 minutes. My previous dishwasher: * Two-tier structure with three rotating water jets (top, middle, bottom). * Separate cutlery drawers, placed in the bottom compartment (making it impossible to wash each spoon separately). * Buttons are on the top of the handle. * The lower plate compartment doesn't fold (you have to play Tetris to place pots in it). * Since there's only one place to put the cutlery, you have to put both solids and liquids in the same place (they sometimes fall out). There were some big differences for me. First, the buttons! The buttons on the LG one are a bit inconvenient. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. It's not necessarily true that more expensive models have better cleaning power. If you're going to buy a model without a filter, I recommend it. Time: LG's standard was 1 hour and 33 minutes. I'm very satisfied :) When I moved, I left my old dishwasher behind and bought a new one for my new home! My old one was a Chef*Rexion, but this time I wanted an LG dishwasher! Even though I use a good dishwasher, I only use standard models, so I checked the price range and ordered it on Coupang! The white color matches my current kitchen! My previous owner also had an LG dishwasher, so I had a spare. The technician just installed it. I'll compare it to my old dishwasher. LG. *3-tier structure - 2 turntables (bottom, middle). The top one seems to only dispense water. *Cutlery and utensil wash compartments are on the top (they wash individual spoons and chopsticks). *Buttons are located on the front, near the handle. *The lower plate compartment folds down (making it easy to load pots). *There's a separate compartment for solid detergent. My previous dishwasher: * Two-tier structure with three rotating water jets (top, middle, bottom). * Separate cutlery drawers, placed in the bottom compartment (making it impossible to wash each spoon separately). * Buttons are on the top of the handle. * The lower plate compartment doesn't fold (you have to play Tetris to place pots in it). * Since there's only one place to put the cutlery, you have to put both solids and liquids in the same place (they sometimes fall out). There were some big differences for me. First, the buttons! The buttons on the LG one are a bit inconvenient. They're on the front and are touch-sensitive, so while I was cleaning the kitchen, I touched them and must have kept touching the cancel button. It canceled, so I had to restart the cycle. Since then, I've always made sure to lock the buttons as soon as I start the cycle! You have to experience this to understand. My previous one had top-mounted buttons, so it never canceled during a cycle. Conclusion: If you're satisfied with the price and don't plan on using many features, this one is a good choice. It also has a high-temperature drying function. The installer, an LG engineer, called to coordinate a date and installed the machine. I'm satisfied. It's not necessarily true that more expensive models have better cleaning power. If you're going to buy a model without a filter, I recommend it. Time: LG's standard was 1 hour and 33 minutes. Sentence (English): Pleasantly surprised!
Comments (English): [ Nice machine, IMHO ] || ---------------- || Pleasantly surprised! Much quieter than I expected. Hemmed and hawed about maybe spending a little more and stepping up to the next level of quietness rating. Glad I didn't as this one is virtually silent, even with us sitting about 12' away in an open floorplan (Great room). We had the upgraded line of Hotpoint appliances installed when we built the house in '06, and this machine is vastly quieter.Cleans well so far. Though I was concerned before purchase, we've had no issues with drying as others seem to be reporting. (Either normal or sensor wash and we do leave the regular heated dry turned on.)Not having one before, I was also surprised how much I liked the 3rd rack. It's a good catch all for odd things that used to take up too much space in the upper rack on the old machine. (Tumbler lids, BBQ tongs, even small bowls)Installation was simple and I didn't need to run out for any "extras." All was includedI'm knocking off one start for something that's more an issue for me and may not be for you. The old machine had a little jog in the 1st rack plate holders. It allowed normal plates to lean back a little bit and our heavy stoneware plates with a deeper edge rim to stand straight. This new one has just straight vertical plate holders. Our heaver/deeper plates tend to want to fall forward when stacking. No biggie. I'm hoping it functions well for a long time. Seems as well built if not a little better than the unit it replaced. But these days, who knows?

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is overall good and is very quiet.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher, finicky "auto-air" feature ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is overall good and is very quiet. But a word of warning - if you live in an old house as I do where things aren't completely level, you may have an issue with the "auto air" feature, which opens the door to air out automatically when it's done. A nice feature when it works but it wasn't working when it was first installed and several repair people came from Bosch to fix it. One unfortunately damaged the dishwasher (broke one of the leveling legs) which the next guy had to replace. Ultimately they got it working, and the repairs were covered under the warranty but I think it's only a matter of time before it stops working again. Google "auto air not working" and you'll see lots of threads online about the problem. If I had known how sensitive it was beforehand -- one repair guy said it would only really work if the floor was 100% level, good luck finding that in a 100 year old house -- then I would have probably got a different model or brand.

Sentence (English): We had a Bosch dishwasher for maybe 10 years and were very pleased.
Comments (English): [ A mind of it's own ] || ---------------- || We had a Bosch dishwasher for maybe 10 years and were very pleased. We bought it from a friend who was remodeling and wanted stainless instead of black. We were very pleased with the performance and durability of the appliance. We were at Lowe's recently and in the bargin aisle was a new dishwasher on sale because it was a demo. We bought it and because it was on sale, we had to bring it home ourselfs. I installed it several days later because it didn't have all the parts required. I bought a new supply hose and electrical junction box, leveled it up and secured it. So far, so good. The users manual was not with the unit so we downloaded it from your site. I have read and re-read it numerous times but the machine does not want to do what we wish it to do. Most of the time it will only do a load in Auto cycle, no matter how many times we try anything else. I just now started a load and it actually went to standard cycle, however it would not accept the air day add on. This was one of the selling points and it has only worked once. It does an amazing job cleaning the dishes but it just seams to have a mind of it's own. My layman's opinion is that either it is operator error, (it does seem to be a more complicated procedure than many others) or it was somehow set to demo mode and needs to be reset to normal or the computer is defective. Maybe someone with more knowledge can suggeat something to correct this situation.

Sentence (English): We recently purchased an 800 series dishwasher from bestbuy and had it installed by their installers.
Comments (English): [ New dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We recently purchased an 800 series dishwasher from Best Buy and had it installed by their installers. The dishwasher worked once and then went completely dead ( no power) but oddly didn't trip the circuit breaker. Their repair guy came and thought maybe it came unplugged from power source. He noted the power cord was wrapped around the leg of the dishwasher, which he fixed. My dishwasher was now working well until a week or so later we noted a strong smell of plastic burning. The dishwasher didn't have any power again but again our circuit breaker for the dishwasher did not trip? Another call was made to Best Buy in which they replaced the dishwasher. During the removal of the old washer noted that the junction box that was supplied by Bosch was burned and the middle ground wire was completely burnt! The installer was amazed that happened and could of caused a severe house fire! They installed the new dishwasher and as of now it is working well. But since they used another Bosch supplied junction box, I'm frightened to use the dishwasher without being home and I must be awake and be near in case it catches fire,again! This is not something I should have to do after spending 1300 dollars for nice dishwasher! I will now have to incur the cost of hiring an electrician to place an outlet under my sink in order to plug it in instead of using the hard wire fix with a faulty, dangerous junction box!

Sentence (English): This is a fabulous dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher. Terrible installer. ] || ---------------- || This is a fabulous dishwasher. I am so happy with its ability to clean, and how spacious it is. I loved my old dishwasher and was reluctant to give it up. When its motor burned out, I decided it was time to shop for another one. This GE dishwasher checked all my boxes and gave me boxes. I didn't even know I needed. Having the third rack on top is great for utensils. The jet washers are fabulous for cleaning out stained coffee cups and bottles. The lower rack is big enough to hold my giant cooking bowls. The runtime is longer than what I'm used to but it is low energy and does a fabulous job. My only huge issue was the installer was terrible. if you read other reviews, many customers have the same problem. The first installation date they canceled on a Sunday with less than 24 hours notice so I was unable to reschedule my Monday to be able to work. They assured me my next installation date which was four days later would be the first of the day. I received confirmation that the installation would be between 730 and 9:30 in the morning. The installer called at 11:45 to say that they would be there within 30 minutes. Unfortunately I had an appointment at 12:30 and was unable to be there . The next time they also gave me two weeks later was also a first in the morning appointment. The installer showed up at 11:45 having already done five jobs. He then looked underneath the dishwasher said that it was hardwired in and that he couldn't use the plug, which was under the sink because it would only turn on when the garbage disposal was turned on. While the dishwasher was hardwired in, the plug under the sink was just fine and the hard wiring was easily removable. I had them leave the dishwasher and had somebody install it privately, who was able to get everything done without complication. Wasted two days of work with their installer and likely would have wasted more if I'd had them come back repeatedly. Buy the dishwasher get your own installer.

Sentence (English): Really haven't had a completely properly functioning dishwasher since I got this unit in October.
Comments (English): [ Samsung 39dBA top control dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || Really haven't had a completely properly functioning dishwasher since I got this unit in October. Seems the new discharge hose is about 6 inches shorter than the previous hose that came with the Kenmore I replaced. The install tech joined the two hoses together to make it work. Putting two hoses together apparently causes problems with drainage and it leaves water standing in the basin from time to time, so I notified Samsung Customer service to find a fix. Still waiting for that fix. They were sending out a tech prior to Thanksgiving, but then canceled it for some unknown reason, so I had the pleasure of hand washing the thanksgiving dinner dishes for 12 people. Thanks again Samsung. I will say that this unit, in the few times I have run it, is amazingly quiet. You have to lean down next to the unit to hear if it's running. It does seem to clean the dishes, but I'm one of those old school pre-rinsers, so I'm not sure about hard core dirty dishes. Also, I'm no fan of the control panel. The touch feature for the start button is finicky and normally requires several attempts to get the machine to turn on. The other buttons seem to operate with a single touch. This unit seems smaller than my previous Kenmore as well. So, if you want quiet, this unit is quiet. Make sure you know the length of the discharge hose because I think they've made them shorter to save a few bucks. Samsung customer service has been attentive and supportive for the most part, but the best customer service is never needing customer service. I hope to get this resolved soon. Wonder if I would have had the same trouble with the Bosch unit.

Sentence (English): The mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area from the bottom rotating sprayer, along the floor of the wash area, up the back wall of the wash area to the top rotating sprayer had a leak.
Comments (English): [ Covered not covered ] || ---------------- || The mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area from the bottom rotating sprayer, along the floor of the wash area, up the back wall of the wash area to the top rotating sprayer had a leak. The leak was on the heater element side of the supply along the floor area of the wash area. Evidently, the leak was allowing too much water into the wash area. This additional water was exiting through the top of the breather tube for the heating element. This additional water was populating in the pan below and outside of the wash area. The water was causing the emergency cutoff float (foam disk) to elevate and trigger a continuous drain of the wash area. I was told by Bosh (on the phone) there was no recall. I convinced them to come out, for free, and inspect the washer. They sent a third-party company out. The inspection showed the defect - the heater's exhaust blows along the bottom of the wash area. The heat weakens the mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area causing it to fail (puts a hole in the side of the supply line). The third-party rep said it is an ongoing problem and there is an unofficial recall. He came back a week later and installed a new mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area. This new one has a protective sleeve to prevent the problem. I almost went out and bought a new dishwasher, and it wasn't going to be a Bosh. PS this happened almost three years to the date that installed the dishwasher. The repair cost me time - something move valuable than money. I am happy now. Mostly because it didn't have to waste any more time. Ironically, I'm wasting time writing this :) Hope it helps someone.

The leak was on the heater element side of the supply along the floor area of the wash area. Evidently, the leak was allowing too much water into the wash area. This additional water was exiting through the top of the breather tube for the heating element. This additional water was populating in the pan below and outside of the wash area. The water was causing the emergency cutoff float (foam disk) to elevate and trigger a continuous drain of the wash area. I was told by Bosh (on the phone) there was no recall. I convinced them to come out, for free, and inspect the washer. They sent a third-party company out. The inspection showed the defect - the heater's exhaust blows along the bottom of the wash area. The heat weakens the mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area causing it to fail (puts a hole in the side of the supply line). The third-party rep said it is an ongoing problem and there is an unofficial recall. He came back a week later and installed a new mostly flat plastic L-shaped water supply running inside the wash area. This new one has a protective sleeve to prevent the problem. I almost went out and bought a new dishwasher, and it wasn't going to be a Bosh. PS this happened almost three years to the date that installed the dishwasher. The repair cost me time - something move valuable than money. I am happy now. Mostly because it didn't have to waste any more time. Ironically, I'm wasting time writing this :) Hope it helps someone.

Sentence (English): The Bosch 800 series dishwasher has exceeded my expectations.
Comments (English): [ Very pleased ] || ---------------- || The Bosch 800 series dishwasher has exceeded my expectations. It has been one month and I have used about 40 cycles. (I know this because I downloaded the App and connected it to my wifi.) The App also tells you when cycles are finished. There is a red light at the bottom, to also let you know when it's running if you don't download the App, otherwise it's very quiet. The automatic is the best setting so far it because it adjusts the cleaning time (mostly 1hr 40 min to 2 hours) based on the level of dirtiness. The half full cycle is also a great feature to save water. The 60 minute is a lifesaver when you have more than a sink full of dishes. It completely cleans your dishes, but not completely dry, more dry than you'd expect in a short cycle. When I place dishes and pots into dishwasher where I have just wiped away excess food particles, they come out clean so no water rinse is needed! Bosch does not disappoint as they come out squeaky clean, even if food is dried on. Starchy residue also comes off, even if it's dried on! I believe that is the point, save water and let the dishwasher do the cleaning. I do use the recommended jet dry pod as well as the rinse agent. In addition, Bosch included a water hardness tester. My water was borderline hard and decided to buy and added the 'dishwasher salt'. There are no water spots, however there were none before I added the 'salt'. One thing to note, the new drying element does not 'melt' nor warp my plastic Tupperware containers or lids. One thing to note, there are times when a small amount of water might pool on the top of cups, but I think I have to make sure they are on an angle when loading. The only thing I would change about the dishwasher is the second level configuration. The design doesn't allow for the placement of many glasses because they've added a section to place long stem glassses. I believe the inside is also a little bit smaller than standard dishwashers, however overall dimensions/size is the same. Overall, I would 100% buy this 800 series Bosch again and give it 5 stars!

Sentence (English): We had been in the market for a Bosch 800 dishwasher for a long time and finally made the purchase through Costco.
Comments (English): [ Returning LOUD Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We had been in the market for a Bosch 800 dishwasher for a long time and finally made the purchase through Costco. One thing we were surprised by was the loudness of this supposed "quiet" dishwasher. There is no need for the red dot to prove that the dishwasher is running - you can hear it loud and clear from another room. There is also a clanking noise when the dishwasher is running. We had a service technician out to fix the problem, but it did not help. One thing to note is that this machine does not come with a standard insulation blanket around the machine. I think this is part of the loudness. Another thing we were surprised by was the difficulty in loading the machine compared to our old non-Bosch machine. The tines are spaced in a way that makes it difficult to load of our items, especially bowls. We are returning the machine and going with a different brand. Too bad b/c I know many people who are happy with their Bosch. This specific model of Bosch 800 (the UC is an ADA model and apparently doesn't come with an insulation blanket) is not worth the high price. IN ADDITION to this: the machine was not installed properly. It came unattached to the cabinet sides within a few days, and was not centered (there were gaps on both sides). The repairman helped re-install. On the plus side. I mean, it cleaned the dishes.

Sentence (English): The Bosch SHP9PCM5N Benchmark dishwasher is by far the quietest dishwasher on the market.
Comments (English): [ Quietest dishwasher on the market ] || ---------------- || The Bosch SHP9PCM5N Benchmark dishwasher is by far the quietest dishwasher on the market. When I set a decibel meter 3' away from it, it actually stayed around 38 - 39 dbA. It does not get above a hushed tone every in its cycles. I recently tried out a Cafe dishwasher that was rated at 39 dbA and it regularly registered at 42 dbA and had numerous 1 minute long spikes of 46 dbA (at 3 feet away). Apparently GE (Cafe) does not measure their dishwashers with the same standards as Bosch. So, I returned the Cafe model and bought this Bosch model. The only regret I have is that the racks in this Bosch model are not nearly as nice as those in the Cafe model. I would recommend to Bosch that they stop trying to save money and increase profits by putting cheap racks in otherwise excellent (and expensive) dishwashers. Out of all the dishwashers that my wife and I looked at in Best Buy (in the $1000 and up price range), the Bosch ones had the lowest quality racks. In the end, I decided that I could live with the lower quality racks and that the silent operation and excellent reputation for quality were more important.

Después de realizar la instalación, llenar de sal descalcificadora el depósito, poner el abrillantador, etc. decidí realizar un prelavado de 15 minutos para probarlo y, como se puede comprobar en el vídeo adjunto, el lavavajillas perdía agua por la parte inferior izquierda debido a una grieta interna en el plástico, como puede verse en la foto. Ya he tramitado la devolución con Amazon; pero creo que debería existir un servicio que te permitiese reponer el lavavajillas defectuoso/dañado por el nuevo en la misma entrega. Ahora tendrán que venir a llevarse éste y luego tendré que volver a realizar la compra y volver a quedar con el transportista para realizar otra entrega... ¿Por qué no se puede realizar todo este proceso en una única recogida/entrega? Se ahorrarían costes, viajes, contaminación y se ganaría en eficiencia y rapidez.

Sentence (English): I already had a dish dryer, so I deliberated for a long time before finally deciding on a Samsung product because of its great value.
Comments (English): I already had a dish dryer, so I deliberated for a long time before finally deciding on a Samsung product because of its great value. So, I brought home a dishwasher lady this time. Product Color: They said it was white, but it isn't white. Anyway, it has a grayish tint. Product Design: It has a simple rectangular, square shape. The front is finished with tempered glass, making it very simple yet luxurious. Service/Installation: Two Samsung technicians came and installed it very kindly. I am very satisfied. Functions: I haven't actually used it yet, but the technician drove it briefly and it worked very well. I need to pile up some dishes quickly to give it a try. The 12-place setting is spacious, so it seems like it will be very good for washing dishes. However, there are comments saying that while a 12-place dishwasher is good for large loads, it can be difficult to run when the amount is small. I also thought it might be inconvenient during a move. I am satisfied with this product because of the price and the fact that I can wash small loads without feeling burdened. (For reference, I am a family of four.) Conclusion: It used to be stressful when I was busy and the amount of dishes piled up. Many people say that hiring a dishwasher "Auntie" is a whole new world, so I decided to get one. I hope that thanks to her, I can finally escape some stress. ~ After 2 weeks of use. Noise: Some people say the running sound is loud, but you should expect it to be about the same as a washing machine. The noise level when draining the water is almost on par with a washing machine. With a washing machine, you can keep it in the laundry room and close the door so you don't hear it running, but since a dishwasher is placed in the kitchen, you have to accept the noise with your whole ears. If dishes are placed upside down or standing upright like plates, or if spoons and chopsticks are cleaned well, but if dishes are stacked, the cleaning isn't perfect and water pools, so I have to take them out, wash them again, and dry them in the dryer. Overall Impression: I hired a dishwasher "Auntie" for convenience, but the washing time is a bit slow, and since she doesn't clean the dishes perfectly, it requires a bit of extra effort. ~ I guess I'll have to make do with this until a dishwasher comes out that addresses these downsides (noise, perfect cleaning, and washing time). ~

Functions: I haven't actually used it yet, but the technician drove it briefly and it worked very well. I need to pile up some dishes quickly to give it a try. The 12-place setting is spacious, so it seems like it will be very good for washing dishes. However, there are comments saying that while a 12-place dishwasher is good for large loads, it can be difficult to run when the amount is small. I also thought it might be inconvenient during a move. I am satisfied with this product because of the price and the fact that I can wash small loads without feeling burdened. (For reference, I am a family of four.) Conclusion: It used to be stressful when I was busy and the amount of dishes piled up. Many people say that hiring a dishwasher "Auntie" is a whole new world, so I decided to get one. I hope that thanks to her, I can finally escape some stress. ~ After 2 weeks of use. Noise: Some people say the running sound is loud, but you should expect it to be about the same as a washing machine. The noise level when draining the water is almost on par with a washing machine. With a washing machine, you can keep it in the laundry room and close the door so you don't hear it running, but since a dishwasher is placed in the kitchen, you have to accept the noise with your whole ears. If dishes are placed upside down or standing upright like plates, or if spoons and chopsticks are cleaned well, but if dishes are stacked, the cleaning isn't perfect and water pools, so I have to take them out, wash them again, and dry them in the dryer. Overall Impression: I hired a dishwasher "Auntie" for convenience, but the washing time is a bit slow, and since she doesn't clean the dishes perfectly, it requires a bit of extra effort. ~ I guess I'll have to make do with this until a dishwasher comes out that addresses these downsides (noise, perfect cleaning, and washing time). ~
